new_events.summary: Reuters, citing two sources, reported Exxon CEO Darren Woods and Chevron upstream president Clay Neff cancelled travel to ADIPEC in Abu Dhabi over security concerns. Companies declined comment; event organiser said 120+ US firms would still exhibit. This establishes reported executive nonattendance, not cancellation of the event, a new attack on UAE or an operational order.

OFAC General License FF-1 replaces and supersedes FF dated October 15, authorizing narrowly defined wind-down transactions involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (Iraq Development Bank) and majority-owned entities through 12:01 a.m. EST December 1, 2026; payment to blocked persons must enter blocked accounts. This is limited wind-down permission, not removal of designation or blanket sanctions relief. Exact publication hour not established.

new_events.actor: Gaza hospital health officials / Israeli military
new_events.summary: AP reported hospital officials said an Israeli strike on a civilian vehicle in central Gaza killed two and wounded one. Israel's military had not commented in that report. Reported deaths and strike attribution remain source-attributed; exact occurrence/publication hour and whether a pre-existing event identity exists require deduplication.

existing_event_updates.summary: Reuters reports US Energy Department awarded about 16.8m barrels in loan contracts on Oct 28 to Gunvor, Trafigura, Phillips 66 and Vitol; an earlier 23.8m-barrel tranche was awarded Oct 13. Approximately 40m barrels of borrowing agreements complete the previously offered US SPR tranche. These are loan contract awards, not proof all barrels have been physically drawn or returned. US wider 172m commitment and 400m IEA aggregate are separate denominators.

Reuters interviewed affected patients and medical staff; Red Cross reported facilities treating up to 700 war wounded in a week. About half of 281,000 newly displaced Yemenis since August are in Taiz governorate; the area has been largely isolated since October 3. UN and aid agencies cite medicine, oxygen, fuel, anesthetic and maternity-service shortages. These are distinct indicators, not a new independent casualty total.

AP reports Saudi authorities said they intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed toward Riyadh. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed attacks on Saudi oil sites, airports and military targets without specifying precise attack times; Saudi government had not confirmed the claimed impacts. Keep intercept report separate from claimed impacts and from any prior Ras Tanura incident.

Reuters and AP reported Iran acknowledged receipt of a message from Vice President Vance and had not responded; Trump characterized the outreach as concerning medical supplies while US media attributed it to renewed peace talks. Iranian parliament speaker reiterated the seven-condition framework. Reuters publication at 11:38 ET predates this window, so it is retained as context/late discovery, not a new in-window diplomatic breakthrough.

claims_and_corrections.claim: Three unidentified oil tankers struck mines and caught fire while taking an unauthorized Hormuz route.
claims_and_corrections.contrary_or_independent_evidence: AP could not confirm vessel identities, casualties, incident count or mechanism. Do not equate with the later reported Louise 1 strike.

claims_and_corrections.claim: IRGC electronically captured and landed an American MQM-170 Outlaw drone near Hormuz.
claims_and_corrections.contrary_or_independent_evidence: US CENTCOM spokesman Tim Hawkins called the claim false. No independent drone wreckage/serial/geolocation confirmation established.

claims_and_corrections.claim: Missiles and drones struck Saudi oil refineries, production sites, airports and military targets and caused casualties.
claims_and_corrections.contrary_or_independent_evidence: AP says spokesman did not give precise occurrence times and Saudi authorities had not confirmed the alleged impacts. Saudi interception statements do not independently establish target damage.

claims_and_corrections.claim: No Taiz siege; food and humanitarian access remain open.
claims_and_corrections.contrary_or_independent_evidence: Reuters reports blocked humanitarian supplies and WFP inability to reach 600,000 aid-dependent people per AP; preserve different definitions of access and do not infer all routes uniformly closed.

claims_and_corrections.claim: Arab-led parties stole votes or benefited from foreign interference.
claims_and_corrections.contrary_or_independent_evidence: AP reports election committee inquiry into unspecified foreign interference did not identify Arab-led parties; election results/coalition negotiations must remain separate from unproven allegations.

economic_energy_updates.summary: Energy Department reported award of roughly 40m barrels of borrowing contracts across Oct 13 and Oct 28 tranches. This is completion of awards under an existing 172m US commitment, not 40m additional barrels above that commitment; future 44m interest barrels and repayment timing are administration projections.

Two US oil-major executive trips reportedly cancelled due to security concerns. Event organiser still expects broad participation; do not equate this with UAE infrastructure damage or conference cancellation.

WSJ reported Thursday price declines amid diplomatic speculation; exact contract/settlement timestamps require primary exchange confirmation. Do not treat this as a definitive same-contract daily close or infer price causality.
